name: Kraków
title: Kraków for New Year
lead: 28 December – 2 January, New Year in Kraków.

stay.label: Airbnb
stay.name: Apartment near Czysta street, 15 minutes' walk from the Main Square

facts: Out: Ryanair FR 8976, Mon 28 Dec, Sofia 11:40 → Kraków 12:20. Back: FR 8975, Sat 2 Jan, Kraków 07:00 → Sofia 09:50. Kraków is one hour behind Bulgaria.
The Airbnb is between Czarnowiejska and Czysta streets, west of the Old Town. The map pin is approximate; use the address from the Airbnb app.
Sunrise around 7:35, sunset around 15:40. The best light is around 15:00.
Usually between −4 and 2 °C, often grey, with snow or sleet some days. Every outdoor stop has a plan B. Bring warm, waterproof shoes.
Most of the plan is on foot. Trams: buy tickets at the machine inside the tram by card; plan with the Jakdojade app. For seven people, use two Bolt or Uber cars.
The Main Square Christmas market is expected to run until about 1 January 2027; check krakow.pl.

Kraków bans fireworks from 2026, and the city does not run a fireworks show. Drinking alcohol in public is illegal and fined. Shops close early on 31 December and almost everything is closed on 1 January, so do the big shop on 30 December. Small Żabka shops are often open.
Polish złoty (PLN). Cards work almost everywhere; milk bars and small places can be cash only.
note: The maps are approximate, not to scale, and routes are straight lines between stops. Ridden legs (tram, taxi, plane) are not counted in the distance. For the real street route use the “Open route” button. Opening hours, prices and dates come from public sources and may change; holiday hours around 31 December and 1 January especially. The “Photos” links open an image search.

days.title: Land, check in and a first evening
days.theme: The flight lands at 12:20. Get to the apartment, eat next door, check in and rest. In the evening a short walk through the Old Town, dinner and one drink.

stops.name: Land at Kraków Airport (KRK)
stops.d: Ryanair FR 8976 lands at 12:20, Kraków time (one hour behind Bulgaria). Easiest for seven people with bags: two Bolt or Uber cars straight to the apartment, about 25–35 minutes. Cheaper: the airport train to Kraków Główny (about 20 minutes; buy tickets at the machine on the platform), then a 20-minute walk or a short taxi.
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice

stops.name: Late lunch next to the apartment
stops.d: Eat first if the apartment is not ready yet. Check the check-in time in the Airbnb app and ask the host if you can leave bags earlier.

opts.s: old-school milk bar right by the apartment: soups, pierogi, cutlets, very cheap; pay at the counter
vegan Asian bowls and ramen, 5 minutes' walk
pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap

stops.name: Check in and put your feet up
stops.d: Unpack, rest, sleep after the early start. The sun sets around 15:40 anyway. On the way in, buy water, breakfast things and drinks at a small shop (Żabka) nearby.

stops.name: Planty park and the Collegium Maius courtyard
stops.d: Ten minutes on foot: through the Planty, the green ring around the Old Town, to the Gothic courtyard of the oldest university building (Jagiellońska 15). The courtyard is free; the gate usually closes in the evening, so if it is shut, look through the gate and carry on.

b.name: Bunkier Café, Plac Szczepański 3a
b.d: Skip the park and walk straight down Karmelicka to Plac Szczepański; warm up on the covered, heated terrace of Bunkier Café, then go on to the square.

stops.name: Christmas market on the Main Square
stops.d: The market is expected to stay until about 1 January (check krakow.pl). Have a grzaniec (mulled wine) and try oscypek, smoked sheep's cheese with cranberry. Prices on the square are high, so have dinner elsewhere. On the hour, listen for the trumpet call (hejnał) from St Mary's tower.

stops.name: Dinner off the square
stops.d: Book a table for seven; December evenings fill up.

opts.s: Polish dishes in a brick cellar, plus a cheap salad bar upstairs
highlander (góral) food at long wooden tables, good for groups, live folk music some nights
opts.q: Morskie Oko restauracja Plac Szczepański 8 Kraków

opts.s: cheap Polish home cooking, soup and pierogi, students' favourite

stops.name: One drink on the way home
stops.d: All three are between the square and the apartment.

opts.s: bar and small club with a hidden courtyard, DJs at weekends; 5 minutes from the apartment
craft beer bar in the Tytano complex, a former tobacco factory, 3 minutes from the apartment
legendary cabaret cellar under a palace on the square; check if there is a show
opts.q: Piwnica pod Baranami Rynek Główny 27 Kraków

stops.name: Back to the apartment
stops.d: Five to fifteen minutes on foot from any of the bars.

days.title: Wawel, Kazimierz and a sunset on Krakus Mound
days.theme: A local market, the quiet streets up to Wawel Hill, lunch in Kazimierz, then over the footbridge to Podgórze for sunset from the oldest mound in the city. Dinner and bars in Kazimierz.

stops.name: Leave the apartment
stops.d: Walk north-east along Czysta and Basztowa to the market, about 12 minutes.

stops.name: Stary Kleparz market
stops.d: Locals' food market since the Middle Ages, open Monday to Saturday from early morning: fruit, pickles, cheese, sausage and pączki (Polish doughnuts). Partly covered.

stops.name: Breakfast in the Old Town
stops.d: Three places on the way south.

opts.s: candle-lit café tucked into a side street, with the Loch Camelot cabaret cellar below
all-day breakfasts, a modern take on the milk bar
old bohemian café, hot chocolate and cake

stops.name: St Francis Basilica and Kanonicza Street
stops.d: Free. Look up at Stanisław Wyspiański's stained-glass window 'God the Father' over the entrance. Then walk down Kanonicza, the quietest and oldest street in the Old Town, to the foot of Wawel.
stops.q: Bazylika św. Franciszka z Asyżu Kraków

stops.name: Wawel Hill, then the river path to Skałka
stops.d: Walk up to Wawel from the end of Kanonicza. The castle courtyards and the hill are free; the cathedral, state rooms and Dragon's Den are paid, and on 1 January many of them may be closed, so today is the day. Leave by the path down to the Vistula and walk along the river to Skałka, a Pauline church on a rock with a crypt where Polish poets and painters are buried. Few tourists get this far.

b.name: Wawel Cathedral
b.d: Spend the time indoors: the coronation cathedral, the royal tombs in the crypt and the climb to the Sigismund Bell. Paid; check hours on katedra-wawelska.pl.

stops.name: Lunch in Kazimierz
stops.d: Cheap and quick, to leave time for the sunset.

opts.n: Zapiekanki at the Okrąglak, Plac Nowy
opts.s: the round market hall in the middle of the square: long open baguettes with mushrooms and cheese, the local street food
self-service Polish canteen: soups, pierogi, cutlets
small Polish bistro with home-style dishes

stops.name: Kazimierz courtyards and the Bernatek footbridge
stops.d: Walk Józefa and Szeroka streets and look into the courtyards. Then cross the Bernatek footbridge with its hanging acrobat sculptures to Podgórze.

stops.name: Sunset from Krakus Mound
stops.d: About 20 minutes uphill from the bridge. Free, open all the time, with a 360° view over the city; the sun sets around 15:40. Locals come here, tourists rarely do. The path gets muddy, so wear good shoes. On the way down, pass Ghetto Heroes Square with its 70 empty chairs.

b.name: MOCAK, Lipowa 4
b.d: Museum of Contemporary Art in the old Schindler factory complex, 15 minutes from the bridge. Check opening hours.

stops.name: Dinner in Kazimierz
stops.d: Book for seven. Between sunset and dinner, rest in a café or go back to the apartment by tram.

opts.s: Polish food and house-flavoured vodkas
small home-cooking place, big portions
bistro across the footbridge in Podgórze
opts.q: Zakładka Food and Wine Józefińska 2 Kraków

stops.name: Kazimierz bars
stops.d: Three of the classic Kazimierz bars, two minutes apart.

opts.s: candle-lit rooms, mismatched furniture, concerts in the cellar
huge bar in a former prayer house, with old murals on the walls
dark, candle-lit rooms and old furniture

stops.name: Back to the apartment
stops.d: Two Bolt or Uber cars take about 10 minutes; or walk 30 minutes north through the Old Town (Józefa → Stradomska → Grodzka → the Main Square → Karmelicka).

days.title: Nowa Huta, the communist model town
days.theme: A tram ride east to Nowa Huta, the planned socialist-realist town built in the 1950s: a grand square, a milk bar unchanged since the 1950s and a church shaped like an ark. Back by mid-afternoon for the big shop before the holidays, then a club night.

stops.name: Breakfast near the apartment
stops.d: All within 5 minutes.

opts.s: roastery café with good breakfasts, 5 minutes from the apartment
café of the Bunkier Sztuki gallery with a covered, heated terrace
French bakery with breakfast all morning

stops.name: Tram to Plac Centralny
stops.d: From the Teatr Bagatela stop, take a tram east to Plac Centralny im. Ronalda Reagana, about 35–40 minutes. Check the line in the Jakdojade app or Google Maps. Buy tickets at the machine inside the tram by card; a 24-hour ticket each covers the whole day.

stops.name: Plac Centralny and Aleja Róż
stops.d: The central square of the town planned in the 1950s, framed by grand socialist-realist blocks. Walk up Aleja Róż (Avenue of Roses), where a Lenin statue stood until 1989.

stops.name: Museum of Nowa Huta
stops.d: Branch of the Museum of Kraków in the former Światowid cinema (Osiedle Centrum E 1): life in the communist years. Check hours on mhk.pl. Guided tours of the Cold-War shelters under the town are run by private companies; book them a day ahead.
stops.q: Muzeum Nowej Huty Światowid Osiedle Centrum E 1 Kraków

stops.name: Arka Pana (Lord's Ark)
stops.d: Twenty minutes' walk north through the housing estates. A modernist church shaped like Noah's ark, finished in 1977 after a 20-year fight with the communist authorities. Free; be quiet during mass.

stops.name: Lunch on the square
stops.d: Back on Plac Centralny. Milk bars are cash only.

opts.n: Bar Mleczny Centralny, Osiedle Centrum C 1
opts.s: milk bar on the square since the early 1950s, soup and a main for very little
opts.q: Bar Mleczny Centralny Nowa Huta Kraków

opts.s: restaurant open since 1956, with the interior to match
Kraków's favourite ice cream, for dessert
opts.q: Good Lood Nowa Huta Aleja Róż Kraków

stops.name: Tram back and the big shop
stops.d: Ride back to Teatr Bagatela. Shops close early on 31 December and nearly all are closed on 1 January, so buy food and drinks for New Year's Eve and New Year's Day now at a supermarket near the apartment. Then rest.

stops.name: Dinner in the Old Town
stops.d: Casual and filling before a night out.

opts.s: burgers, good for a group
Polish classics, duck and pierogi
cheap milk bar, closes early in the evening, so go first
opts.q: Bar Mleczny Pod Temidą Grodzka 43 Kraków

stops.name: Club night
stops.d: Three Old Town clubs within 5 minutes of each other and 15 minutes' walk from the apartment. Check the night's programme and entry fee on their pages.

opts.s: electronic club in a cellar labyrinth
bar and club, from indie to dance nights
big cellar club with two dance floors

stops.name: Back to the apartment
stops.d: 15 minutes on foot from any of the three clubs: Szewska → Karmelicka → Czysta. Walk back together.

days.title: Salwator, Kościuszko Mound and New Year's Eve
days.theme: A late start and a walk west along the river to the mound with the widest view of the city. A nap in the afternoon, dinner, then the evening is blocked for New Year's Eve: pick one of three free options.

stops.name: Leave the apartment
stops.d: Walk south through the Planty to Felicjanek Street, 10 minutes.

stops.name: Brunch by the river
stops.d: Both Felicjanek cafés are two minutes from the Vistula.

opts.s: second-hand English bookshop with a café, cakes and quiches
quirky local café full of wardrobes and old furniture
roastery café with good breakfasts, 5 minutes from the apartment

stops.name: Salwator and the Norbertine convent
stops.d: Walk west along the Vistula to Salwator, an old village inside the city: the fortress-like Norbertine convent on the river and the little wooden church of St Margaret on the hill.

stops.name: Kościuszko Mound
stops.d: Uphill for 25 minutes along Aleja Waszyngtona. The mound stands inside a 19th-century fort; paid entry. On a clear day you can see the Tatra mountains.

b.name: National Museum, Al. 3 Maja 1
b.d: Polish 20th-century art and design, 8 minutes from the apartment. Hours on 31 December may be shorter; check mnk.pl.
b.q: Muzeum Narodowe Gmach Główny Al. 3 Maja 1 Kraków

stops.name: Back across Błonia
stops.d: The huge meadow where the Pope said mass; walk straight across it and through Jordan Park towards the apartment.

b.name: Bus or taxi back
b.d: Skip the meadow and take a Bolt back from the mound, about 10 minutes.

stops.name: Late lunch near the apartment
stops.d: Shops close early today; you shopped yesterday.

opts.s: old-school milk bar right by the apartment: soups, pierogi, cutlets, very cheap; pay at the counter
vegan Asian bowls and ramen, 5 minutes' walk
pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap

stops.name: Nap and get ready
stops.d: Rest before a long night. Charge your phones and agree on a meeting point in case you lose each other at midnight (mobile networks get slow).

stops.name: Dinner before the night
stops.d: Most restaurants serve set New Year's Eve menus that must be booked weeks ahead. If you can't book, cook at the apartment with what you bought yesterday.

opts.s: highlander food, long tables for a group
opts.q: Morskie Oko restauracja Plac Szczepański 8 Kraków

opts.s: Polish dishes in a brick cellar
Polish classics

stops.name: New Year's Eve: pick one
stops.d: This time is blocked for New Year's Eve. All three are free to enter. Kraków bans fireworks from 2026 and the city no longer runs a show; the 2026/27 programme had not been announced in October 2026, so check krakow.pl and pik.krakow.pl in December. Drinking alcohol in public is illegal in Poland, and glass is usually not allowed on the square. Taxis are scarce after midnight; all three are walkable from the apartment.

opts.s: the city's big open-air gathering in front of the Cloth Hall, traditionally free; recent years had a stage or light show and a countdown. 15 minutes' walk from the apartment

opts.n: Plac Nowy and the Kazimierz bars
opts.s: the square in Kazimierz fills up at midnight; bar-hop between Alchemia, Singer and Eszeweria, which usually have no entry fee, though some may sell New Year tickets, so check. 30 minutes' walk
the locals' alternative: watch midnight over the whole city from the top, quiet and free. Bring a torch and warm layers. 40 minutes' walk or 15 by taxi before 23:00

stops.name: Back to the apartment
stops.d: Walk back together; taxis are scarce and expensive after midnight. From the Main Square 15 minutes, from Plac Nowy 30 minutes, from Krakus Mound about 50 minutes (or a taxi if you can get one).

days.title: New Year's Day, slow
days.theme: A public holiday: most shops are closed and many cafés open late. A late brunch, a walk along the river to the cliffs of the Zakrzówek quarry lake, an early dinner and an early night, because the alarm rings at 04:00.

stops.name: Wake up slowly
stops.d: Leave around midday.

stops.name: Late brunch
stops.d: On 1 January opening hours are uncertain; check Google Maps before you go. Przypiecek is open round the clock.

opts.s: pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap
all-day breakfasts, a modern take on the milk bar
French bakery with breakfast all morning

stops.name: Along the Vistula and over the Dębnicki bridge
stops.d: Walk down to the river and cross the Dębnicki bridge for the view back to Wawel from the other bank, then follow the streets of Dębniki south towards Zakrzówek.

b.name: Massolit Books & Café, Felicjanek 4
b.d: Sit out the rain with coffee and cake among second-hand books, two minutes from the bridge. Check that it is open on 1 January.

stops.name: Zakrzówek quarry lake
stops.d: Cross the Dębnicki bridge and walk 25 minutes south to the flooded limestone quarry: turquoise water under white cliffs, with paths along the top. The park is open in winter; the swimming pools are summer-only. Watch the sunset here around 15:45.

b.name: Kino Pod Baranami, Rynek Główny 27
b.d: Arthouse cinema in a palace on the square; films are shown in the original language with Polish subtitles. Check the 1 January programme.

stops.name: Back by tram or taxi
stops.d: From Zakrzówek take a tram towards the centre or two Bolt cars, about 15 minutes to the apartment. Rest and pack.

stops.name: Last dinner
stops.d: In Kazimierz. Book ahead and check that they are open on 1 January.

opts.s: Israeli food, mezze for the table
French bistro, good value
tiny pierogi place with unusual fillings
opts.q: Pierogi MR Vincent Bożego Ciała 12 Kraków

stops.name: One last quiet drink
stops.d: Close to dinner, so you can be home by 22:30.

opts.s: bar with old Singer sewing machines as tables
cosy café-bar opposite Hevre
calm Old Town bar, on the way home

stops.name: Pack and sleep
stops.d: Book two taxis for 04:45 tonight (Bolt or Uber can schedule rides) and set alarms for 04:00.

days.title: Departure
days.theme: Flight FR 8975 leaves at 07:00 and lands in Sofia at 09:50 Bulgarian time.

stops.name: Wake up and check out
stops.d: Leave the keys as the host asked and close the windows.

stops.name: Two taxis to the airport
stops.d: About 20–25 minutes at night. The airport train may start too late at this hour; if you want it, check the first departure on kolejemalopolskie.com.pl.

stops.name: Kraków Airport
stops.d: Check in online with Ryanair before you go. Security can be slow in the morning; the gate closes 30 minutes before departure.
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice

stops.name: Flight to Sofia
stops.d: FR 8975, Kraków 07:00 → Sofia 09:50 (Bulgarian time).
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice
